The observed Alfvénic activity below the TAE frequency is characterized by well-defined frequency lines surrounded by wide (∼15 kHz) frequency bands.
The model used in this paper includes higher-order harmonics of the geodesic field-line curvature caused by plasma shaping, as opposed to just the lower-order toroidicity.
The predicted frequency range of the HOGAEs is ω_GAM ≤ ω ≤ ω_TAE, significantly above the values predicted by previous lower-order coupling models.
The theoretical predictions of HOGAE frequency and radial location are in fair agreement with measurements in JET experiments, with the HOGAEs located in the inner half of the plasma (ρ_pol < 0.5).
Plasma elongation is shown to play an essential role in the high-order coupling model, as it contributes to higher-order harmonics of the geodesic curvature.
The observed HOGAEs have frequencies around one-half of the typical TAE frequency.
A safety factor larger than 2 (or slightly higher if elongation is increased) prevents the HOGAE gaps from opening, limiting their existence to the inner part of the plasma.

The plasma rotation frequency measured from the 3/2 neoclassical tearing mode is used to convert between the AE frequencies computed in the plasma frame and the Doppler-shifted frequencies measured in the experiments.
The HOGAE stability is mainly determined by the interplay between thermal-ion Landau damping and the drive from the anisotropic ICRH-heated ion population.
The authors consider the effects of thermal-ion dilution due to impurities and the fraction of ICRH-heated ions on the balance of energy exchange between the HOGAEs and the plasma species.
The major wave-particle resonances are found to be located at energies close to the plasma temperature at the AE location and the fundamental ICRH resonance for the heated H ions.
The authors employ a hybrid MHD/drift-kinetic code to evaluate the resonant energy exchange between the HOGAEs and the relevant plasma species.
The authors use the EFIT code to reconstruct the magnetic equilibrium and the CASTOR and CASTOR-K codes to compute the continuous spectra and the linear stability of the observed HOGAEs.
The authors analyze two JET plasma scenarios, #90198 and #90199, with the former providing a simpler case for analysis due to the presence of a single, well-separated HOGAE.
The authors use reflectometry and soft X-ray data to constrain the radial location of the observed HOGAEs, finding them to be in the inner half of the plasma.
